title: Design System: Origen MdP — Costa Tech

display.purpose: The hero headline only — Archivo at 119% width, one per page.

headline.purpose: Section titles and region promises: what the business gains, stated first.

body.purpose: Bajadas, detail paragraphs, section text. Held to 42–58ch.

region-name.purpose: The plain-Spanish name of a region wherever it is offered: index rows, selector rows, region subtitles.

label.purpose: Narrow tracked uppercase micro-labels: nav links, field legends, ghost buttons.

lockup.purpose: "Origen MdP — Costa Tech", never split; condenses to 86% width below 560px.

address.purpose: Chivo Mono for every hex address, form input, error string and footer line.

byte.purpose: Chivo Mono for the live byte field's two-digit hex cells. Decorative and aria-hidden.

shadows.name: edge-hairline
shadows.purpose: Bottom edge of an isometric plane, so an unallocated region reads as a real stratum rather than a plane being erased.

shadows.name: edge-hairline-activa
shadows.purpose: The same edge on the active layer.

shadows.name: active-layer-bloom
shadows.purpose: The lifted active layer's cast onto the stack below it. Active state only.

shadows.name: action-bloom
shadows.purpose: Under the primary action at rest, so the one orange rectangle on the page sits off the ground.

shadows.name: action-bloom-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary action hover, paired with a 2px lift.

shadows.name: state-dot-halo
shadows.purpose: Ring around an active index dot, selector dot or confirmation dot.

motion.name: salida
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for the entire page. Exponential ease-out; every transition and keyframe uses it.

motion.name: revela
motion.purpose: Soft sequential reveal from translateY(14px). Hidden state exists only under the .js class an inline head script sets before paint.

motion.name: revela-stagger
motion.purpose: Staggered arrival inside a section, never a global timeline.

motion.name: capa-lift
motion.purpose: Isometric layer fan and the active layer's lift to translateZ(236px).

motion.name: cross-fade-allocacion
motion.value: opacity 700ms var(--salida), filter 700ms var(--salida), transform 700ms var(--salida)
motion.purpose: Noise blurs out at 3px while the allocated structure resolves in the same box.

motion.name: byte-churn
motion.value: rAF loop, ~100ms cadence, 6 cells per tick, 3-tick live decay, color 420ms var(--salida)
motion.purpose: Idle-from-load byte mutation by direct DOM writes. IntersectionObserver-paused offscreen; never started under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: llamada-entrada
motion.purpose: Leader-line callouts slide 10px inward as their layer lifts.

motion.name: estado
motion.purpose: Hover and active state changes on buttons, nav links, cards, dots and fields.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition-duration: 0.01ms; .revela opacity 1 / transform none; .bloqueRegion opacity 1; .contenidoCapa opacity 1
motion.purpose: Every dimmed or hidden state has an explicit reset in the same stylesheet that dimmed it.

layout.name: cabecera
layout.purpose: Sticky header height; anchors carry scroll-margin-top of cabecera + 16px.

layout.name: pila
layout.value: 296px square, rotateX(56deg) rotateZ(-40deg), 26px in-plane / 62px Z per index
layout.purpose: The isometric region stack; 250px with 24px/52px steps below 1100px.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The one orange rectangle in a section: quote request and form submit.

components.name: Field
components.description: Recessed square well; the visitor's typing is set in mono like any other machine value.

components.name: Region Row
components.description: The 01–04 index row and the quote selector row are the same object: dot, number, plain-Spanish name, hex address.

narrative.overview:
The page is a memory map of the visitor's operation. Regions are allocated in ascending address order, and that order is the only law of placement on the surface: nothing sits anywhere because it looked good there. Beneath the allocated regions a field of live bytes keeps churning on its own from the moment the page loads — unclaimed matter, still running by hand. What is sold here is the transition from that noise into structure, so the system's job is to make both states materially present at once and let the visitor watch one become the other.

The world is drawn from the IT and software materials themselves — hex addresses, byte fields, allocated blocks, isometric planes, leader-line callouts — and deliberately refuses the category's default dress. There is no gradient mesh, no glass, no dotted grid, no neon-on-near-black. The ground is tinta, a violet-cast ink that is emphatically not a neutral near-black; the single live accent is a burnt orange with body in it, not a glow. Every region carries its name in plain Spanish at full display size, so the map reads as an offer rather than as wallpaper.

Density is deliberate and unequal: display type is set wide and tight, labels are set narrow and wide-tracked, and monospace carries every address, byte and measurement without exception. Motion is part of the system, not a finish: idle churn, scroll-driven allocation, and staggered reveals are three expressions of one orchestrated behaviour, and all three collapse to a legible resting state under prefers-reduced-motion.
keyCharacteristics: Violet-cast ink ground, never neutral black, never pure black.
One burnt-orange accent, reserved for the active region and the primary action.
One variable type family worked across its width axis (76%–119%), plus one monospace for all machine values.
Zero corner radius everywhere except state dots; hairline rules do the dividing.
Ascending address order governs reading order; every region is numbered 01–04 and addressed in hex.
Motion is idle-from-load, scroll-driven, and reduced-motion-safe by construction.

rules.name: The One Live Region Rule
rules.body: Naranja marks exactly one region at a time, plus the primary action. If two regions are orange at once, the map has stopped saying which one is being explained.

rules.name: The Never-Neutral Ground Rule
rules.body: The ground is violet-cast ink and its three siblings. Pure black, neutral grey, and near-black-with-neon are all out of world; the cast in the ink is what separates this page from the category.

rules.name: The Hueso Tenue Floor Rule
rules.body: Running text never goes dimmer than hueso-tenue. Violeta is a structural colour — borders, bars, markers — and is not a text colour.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Chivo Mono carries every address, byte, measurement and machine-echoed value — including what the visitor types into the form. Prose is never set in mono; a number the machine produced is never set in Archivo.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed on the width axis before it is expressed on size. Labels narrow (76–88%), display wide (119%). Never introduce a second sans family to do what the axis already does.

rules.name: The Plain Name Rule
rules.body: Every region label is plain Spanish at full size, with no cleverness and no abbreviation. The name of the offer is the offer.

rules.name: The Indivisible Lockup Rule
rules.body: "Origen MdP — Costa Tech" is one lockup and is never split across lines or used by halves. On narrow viewports it condenses on the width axis (112% → 86%) and drops to 11.5px rather than breaking.

rules.name: The Ascending Address Rule
rules.body: Placement follows the address. Regions read 0x0000 upward, top to bottom, in every layout — the isometric stack, the index, the flat narrow-viewport map and the quote selector all agree. There is no arbitrary position on this page.

rules.name: The Designed Narrow Rule
rules.body: The phone gets a different instrument, not a squeezed one. The 3D stack does not shrink into a phone; it is replaced by the flat address gutter, and the idle churn survives there at a reduced cell budget.

rules.name: The Lift-Above-All Rule
rules.body: The active layer clears the entire stack (translateZ(236px)), it does not merely step up one rung. A region under discussion is never partially occluded — a byte field seen through a slot is a bug, not a texture.

rules.name: The Accent-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every soft shadow in this system is orange-tinted and state-bound. Neutral drop shadows and hard offset shadows are not part of this world.

dos: Do place by address. Ascending hex order is the only ordering law on this page; every view of the regions must agree with it.
Do keep exactly one region live at a time, in naranja, everywhere it appears at once — plane, callouts, index row, address.
Do set every address, byte, measurement and user-typed value in Chivo Mono with tabular numerals, and everything a person wrote in prose in Archivo.
Do express hierarchy on the width axis first (76% labels → 119% display) before reaching for size or a second family.

Do ship the hidden reveal state behind the .js class that an inline <head> script sets before paint. Content is present and visible without JavaScript, without hydration, and if the observer never fires. This pattern is load-bearing and any new animated reveal must adopt it.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion resting state in the same stylesheet that dims something. Nothing that scroll activation turns on may stay off for a user who cannot scroll it on.
Do keep the byte field decorative and aria-hidden, and keep every region name, address and callout as real text in the accessibility tree.

Do theme the browser's own surfaces from the palette — selection, caret, accent-color, scrollbar track and thumb, :focus-visible, underline offset, tabular numerals. The page does not stop at its own edge.
Do mark missing proof as a designed placeholder in the world's notation (dashed orange hairline, mono label), never as a filled-in stand-in.
donts: Don't use a neutral near-black or pure black ground. The violet cast in tinta is the identity.
Don't treat naranja as a surface colour or a glow. It is a pigment with body, reserved for the live region and the primary action.
Don't set running text, placeholders or addresses in violeta. It is a structural colour for borders, bars and markers.
Don't round a corner. Radius exists only for state dots.
Don't lift an active layer partway. It clears the whole stack or it is not the active layer.
Don't put a callout label inside the 3D space, and don't terminate a leader line in empty ground — the line must land on the lifted plane's measured band.
Don't jack the scroll, scrub a timeline, or make any content depend on an animation in order to be readable.
Don't load type through next/font/google. Both families are self-hosted because that path silently degrades to Arial when the build host cannot reach fonts.gstatic.com.
Don't imply evidence that does not exist — no clients, testimonials, metrics, awards, press or pricing have a visual slot in this system, and none may be invented to fill a layout.
Don't split "Origen MdP — Costa Tech". It condenses on the width axis; it never breaks or appears by halves.
